script: I hit a car—my ex‑bestfriend's sister. Now I am destroyed and stunned… what happens next?. I was driving through the city at 2 a.male., lights blinking, earbuds in, thinking I could handle any traffic. The red light stopped me, I hit the brakes, and boom—a car slammed into my rear, shaking me like a toy truck. (Micro‑hook: The moment my car lurched, I knew I'd have to call someone.) I was frozen, my fingers gripping the wheel, "What the heck?" spilling out before I could even decide what to do. I got out, phone in hand, eyes locked on the other car's window. The driver was a guy I'd seen before—M23, and the passenger was F19, my ex‑bestfriend's little sister, who'd just had a baby a few weeks ago. They were all apologetic, saying "Don't call the police," but I was like, "I can't ignore this. I need to document it for insurance." I snapped photos of the license plate and the dented bumper, then told them to lower their windows so I could see the damage clearly. I felt like I was the only one with the right to complain, the only one who'd actually pay the bill. (Stakes: I had to file a claim, pay for the damage, and I couldn't do it blind.) I called the police. We sat in my car while they arrived, the air thick with tension. When the officers came, we filed the report. The other couple apologized again, "Sorry, sorry," and I told them to be careful, especially with a newborn in the house. I thought I was being responsible, protecting everyone's interests, especially my own. (Tension wave: I was standing firm, but the other side was softening.) The next day, my ex‑bestfriend slid into my DMs like it was a personal attack. She was yelling, "You're ruining our baby's life, you're going to skyrocket our insurance!" I was like, "Seriously? I did what I had to do." She kept saying they were "struggling" and that my report would hurt them. I felt empathy, but I also felt my own right to protect myself. I am not here to be the martyr; I am here to keep my car and my wallet intact. (Open loop: I wondered if I should have just let them go.) I am not saying I am a villain. I was doing what I had to do. I didn't want to be the one who had to pay for a rear‑end because someone else was careless. I didn't want to be the one who'd have to explain to an insurance company that a baby's first cry was caused by a car crash. I was just doing the smart thing. (Reflection: The aftermath was that my ex‑bestfriend was upset, but I knew I was right.) In the end, the police report was filed, the insurance company will sort the damage, and I am left with the knowledge that I did the right thing. If they're upset, fine. I am not here to make them feel guilty. I am here to keep my car, my peace, and my future from being wrecked by someone else's mess.
